ऋषियों ने प्रार्थना कीः हे भगवान्‌, आपके कार्य अत्यन्त आश्चर्यमय हैं और यद्यपि आप सब

सम्पत्ति की देवी लक्ष्मीजी से भी लिप्त नहीं हैं, जिनकी पूजा ब्रह्माजी जैसे बड़े-बड़े देवताओं
द्वारा उनकी कृपा प्राप्त करने के उद्देश्य से की जाती हे |

लिप्त नहीं होते। भगवान्‌ की इस उच्च दिव्य स्थिति का वर्णन अनेक ऋषियों ने विशेष तौर पर किया

The sages prayed: O God, your works are very wonderful, and although you do everything with your various powers, you are not attached to them. Even you
are not even involved with the goddess of wealth, Lakshmiji, whose worship is done by great gods like Brahmaji
with the aim of attaining her grace.

Meaning: It is said in the Bhagavad Gita that God has no desire for the fruits of his wonderful deeds,
nor does he need to perform actions. But to present an example in front of the common people,
he sometimes performs actions, which are extremely astonishing. Not by the actions of the mother.
Even though they perform actions in a very surprising way, they are not attached to any object.
They are self-contained. Here, an example is given that the goddess of wealth,
Lakshmi, is always engaged in the service of God, but even then, she is not attached to them.
Even
gods like Brahma worship her to become worthy of Lakshmi, the goddess of wealth; but,
although hundreds and thousands of wealth goddesses are engaged in the worship of Lord Kou, they are not
engaged with any of them. Lord Kau has described this high divine state in many ways, especially by the sages. They are not like ordinary souls, who are attached to the fruits of their meritorious deeds.

The mind is pacified, the fire of suffering is extinguished.

He who is full of Brahman does not wander. 35). Meaning of the word

Siddhah- Siddho said; Ouchu- prayed; Ayam- that; Tvat- your; Mishra- impure; Piyush- nectar;
Nadyam- in the river; Manah- of the mind; Varnah- elephant; Klesh- suffering; Daw- fire- from the forest fire; Dagdah- burnt; Trusha- thirst;

Siddho praised: O Lord, our minds are like that elephant, which, when distressed by the forest fire,
when immersed in the river, forgets all its sufferings.
Similarly, these are also our minds.
You are immersed in the nectar-river of divine plays, and you want to remain constantly in such divine bliss.
It is like the happiness of becoming one with the Supreme Brahman.

Meaning: This statement is of the inhabitants of Siddhaloka, where eight types of material accomplishments are found. The residents there are the masters of eight types of yoga siddhis, but from their statement, it seems that they are pure devotees. They constantly immerse themselves in the nectar-like stream of listening to the divine plays of God.
The listening to the divine plays of God is called Krishna's story. Similarly, Tg
The Maharaj says that those who remain immersed in the nectar-like ocean of the stories of God's plays
are liberated and they have no fear from material life. Siddham says that a common man's mind
remains full of worries. Here, an example of such an elephant is given, which, distressed by the forest's
fire, enters the river to seek relief.
If people suffering from this world-like fire of desire
enter only into the nectar-lake of the description of the stories of Lord Krishna, then they forget all the sufferings of this
world. Siddham ko sakam karman ki--just as by performing a Yagya, one enjoys good fruits--
they do not care even a little. They remain engrossed in the divine discussion of the Lord's Leelas, and because of this,
they remain very pleased; they do not care whether they perform good or bad deeds. Those who always
remain absorbed in Krishna consciousness, they do not need to perform any kind of actions or yagyas. Krishna bhava namrata is self-absorbed, because it includes all the rituals described in the Vedas.

होते नहीं | वास्तविक श्रेष्ठता तो कृष्ण की है। कृष्णस्तु भगवान्‌ स्वयं--यह वचन श्रीमद्‌भागवत का है।
